title: fp8 E5M2 addition under roundNearestTiesToEven is monotone in its first argument
statement: Let F be the IEEE-754-conformant 8-bit format OCP fp8 E5M2, SMT-LIB `(_ FloatingPoint 5 3)`, and let RNE denote roundNearestTiesToEven. For all values a, b, c of F: if fp.leq(a, b) holds and neither fp.add(RNE, a, c) nor fp.add(RNE, b, c) is NaN, then fp.leq(fp.add(RNE, a, c), fp.add(RNE, b, c)). Note that fp.leq is false whenever either operand is NaN, so the antecedent already excludes NaN inputs; the two explicit guards exclude only NaN RESULTS, which arise from (+oo) + (-oo). This is the property that licenses interval and bound propagation through a rounded-addition kernel.

formal.statement: (assert (=> (and (fp.leq a b) (not (fp.isNaN (fp.add RNE a c))) (not (fp.isNaN (fp.add RNE b c)))) (fp.leq (fp.add RNE a c) (fp.add RNE b c))))

evidence.supports: Every fp8 E5M2 triple (a, b, c) satisfying the antecedent was enumerated -- 7843500 of the 16777216 triples -- and the consequent held at all of them, under RNE and under each of the other four SMT-LIB rounding modes.
evidence.notes: Ran 2026-08-14. examined=7843500 failures=0 at RNE, and identically at RNA, RTP, RTN and RTZ. The enumeration is over all 2^24 = 16777216 triples of the 8-bit format; 7843500 of them pass the guard (fp.leq(a,b) holds and neither result is NaN) and are the ones the claim speaks about. `rustc_apfloat` 0.2.3 (LLVM APFloat) shares no code with axeyum's bit-blaster, CNF encoder or SAT core. Ordering is APFloat's PartialOrd, which is SMT-LIB fp.leq: NaN unordered, +0 and -0 equal. The binary exits non-zero on any violation.

evidence.supports: The negation of formal.statement is unsatisfiable over fp8 E5M2, decided symbolically -- without enumerating the 2^24 triples.
evidence.notes:
Ran 2026-08-14: `; evidence kind=unsat-drat certified=1 recheck=ok arena=ok ms=928629`, verdict `unsat`, 25m46.4s wall in a release build on a machine at load 16-25. `recheck=ok` is axeyum's own `check_drat` (RUP+RAT, ADR-0011) re-checking the emitted refutation; `arena=ok` is `Evidence::check` against a fresh parse.

NO EXTERNAL ORACLE AGREES OR DISAGREES, because neither can read the query: z3 4.13.3 returns `unknown` with `(:reason-unknown "addition/subtract with ebits > sbits not supported")` -- E5M2 is (_ FloatingPoint 5 3) and 5 > 3 -- and bitwuzla 0.9.1 rejects the format as experimental, its own suggested `--fpexp` escape being a BUILD option that the binary refuses as an invalid runtime flag. The independent confirmation is the exhaustive row above, not a second solver.

THIS ROW CARRIES NO `checker_command` ON PURPOSE. At 25m46s it would blow any per-checker budget scripts/check-fact-evidence-replay.sh runs with. The fact stays covered by the exhaustive row, which re-runs in about three seconds. To re-derive this row by hand:
  cargo run --release -q -p axeyum-bench --example smtcomp_cli -- --evidence artifacts/facts/smt2/neg-fp8-add-monotone-rne.smt2

provenance.established_by: fp-kernels lane; an exhaustive LLVM-APFloat enumeration of all 2^24 fp8 E5M2 triples, and independently a symbolic CNF/DRAT refutation from axeyum
provenance.source: authored here. The proposition is the one a bound-propagation or interval-arithmetic pass over a quantized kernel silently assumes.

prior_art.what: That each rounding-direction attribute defines a monotone (non-decreasing) map from the extended reals to the format, so a correctly-rounded operation inherits the monotonicity of the exact operation it rounds.
prior_art.attribution: standard textbook attribution; this lane did not consult the primary source, and records the citation as the received one. Nothing in the evidence above depends on it -- the property is enumerated here, not derived.

notes:
TWO ROUTES, AND NEITHER IS AN EXTERNAL SOLVER. This fact is settled twice: by enumerating every one of the 2^24 fp8 E5M2 triples in about three seconds, and by bit-blasting the guarded miter to CNF and refuting it in 25m46s with a re-checked DRAT proof. Alone in this batch, NEITHER settlement could be cross-checked against z3 or bitwuzla, and that is a measured fact about the field rather than an omission: z3 4.13.3 returns `unknown` on the file with `(:reason-unknown "addition/subtract with ebits > sbits not supported")`, because E5M2 is (_ FloatingPoint 5 3) and 5 > 3; bitwuzla 0.9.1 rejects the format outright as experimental, and the `--fpexp` escape named in its own error message is a BUILD option that the binary refuses as an invalid runtime flag. So axeyum decides, at this width, a claim that neither industrial FP solver can read -- which is the direct consequence of ADR-0023 making the FP builders generic over (exp_bits, sig_bits).

WHY THE EXHAUSTIVE ROW CARRIES THE CHECKER AND THE SYMBOLIC ONE DOES NOT. 3s against 25m46s. The cheap row is also the one that rests on less: it does not go through axeyum's fpa2bv lowering, whose `add` is documented in its own source as a validated rather than proven bit-blaster, nor through Tseitin, nor through the SAT core. The footprint has to assume all three for the symbolic row, and none of them for the enumeration. Two routes agreeing across that gap is the evidence.

THE ARITY WALL. This claim is exhaustive at fp8 and nowhere else. 2^24 triples is seconds; the same claim at binary16 is 2^48 triples and at binary32 is 2^96. Unary claims escape it -- F:fp32-doubling-add-equals-mul-two is enumerated over all 2^32 binary32 values in under a minute -- so it is ARITY, not width, that decides whether brute force is available. The binary16 instance is recorded separately and is still `open`: see F:fp16-add-monotone-rne.

SCOPE. E5M2 only. Nothing here transfers to E4M3, which has no infinities and an all-ones NaN, is therefore not an IEEE format, and which axeyum's `arithmetic_format_supported` gate refuses for exactly that reason.
